method: Question coverage uses a_c=(B_c−P_c)/(B_c−F_c), with B=(250,249,247), F=(37,53,38), edge mean coverage between 0.05 and 0.95, and channel spread=max(a_c)−min(a_c). Native selected-node rect, documentRect, client and offset arrays are compared exactly across implementations before/after each screenshot. Original files are only read.

visualReview.finding: All eight initial native screenshots were inspected at original resolution. They contain the complete painted device arrangement, section heading, action and adjacent page context. The default pixel equality is not produced by blank or offscreen device captures. The flagged environment retains visible text/image-edge raster differences within the device composition.

findings: Both environments retain identical 53 source hashes, 4 protected hashes, 3 harness hashes, 3 build hashes and complete frontend tree identity. The browser patch version and runner image differ, confounding the direct mode comparison.
In each environment all 2,240 selected-node geometry-array comparisons are exact; no selected rect moves during a screenshot. The device stage is fully within every visible-stage viewport.

Default Chromium 155.0.8059.84 uses the retained LCD-like laptop question variant on both pages at every visible stage. All 10 paired full-viewport diagnostic comparisons have zero pixels above the existing 24-channel threshold.

Flagged Chromium 155.0.8059.39 forces scalar/grayscale-like question coverage on both pages. At 1440 both laptop question crops equal the retained 4ee8e4c19d8faf7261b91873bafa716557e394c5fbfbe49d79fce5a0087ef97f RGB variant, but other device regions still differ.

At 901 under the flag both question crops are scalar/grayscale-like but differ from each other despite exact native bounds. The two-mode LCD/grayscale model therefore explains a real component of the earlier failures, but does not exhaust all device raster differences.

The flag retains 9,523 differing device pixels at 901 and 11,705 at 1440, unchanged through scroll and viewport-height round trips. The corresponding device-region ratios are 0.0262267180 and 0.0154533692.

Residual 1440 samples under the flag include 328 changed pixels in the laptop logo,1433 in the sidebar, 2,220 in the answer region and 1,383 in the tablet question; the laptop question, helper, tablet logo and sampled phone region match at the same 24-channel threshold.

recommendation.currentChange: No runtime, CSS, checkpoint threshold, capture mask or browser flag change is justified by this two-job comparison.
recommendation.why: The tested flag does not resolve the full native raster discrepancy, and the default/flag contrast is confounded by different browser patch versions and runner images. One matching default pair is insufficient evidence that a newer Chrome version fixed the root cause.
recommendation.smallestControlledFollowup: A causal comparison of LCD flags would require one exact browser binary and runner for both modes. Such a causal claim is not required for the accepted workflow-only version pin and is not made here.
recommendation.completionGate: Any eventual checkpoint environment correction still requires the full Writing matrix with unchanged assertions and limits, plus explicit documentation of the tested browser environment. Existing failed checkpoints remain preserved.
recommendation.workflowCorrection: The separately reviewed exact official current-Stable Chrome pin is justified as a reproducibility correction. It changes neither runtime styling nor default rendering flags.
recommendation.nextVerification: Run the full unchanged Writing gate using the exact pinned default Chrome. Preserve its complete result and browser metadata. This remains a fresh verification, not a replacement of the original failed evidence.

limits: This analysis does not identify the compositor event, cache state or transform transition responsible for the residual pixels.
The eight inspected initial screenshots are a visual sample; geometry and crop analysis cover every recorded stage.
The alpha-coverage marker0.05 is diagnostic only and does not alter the checkpoint pixel tolerance.
No runtime, harness, CSS or original PNG files were changed by this diagnostic review.
